label: Kasseri
note: Kashkaval (Balkans) and kaşar (Turkey) are the same kind of cheese

about.text: Kasseri is a Greek pasta filata cheese made from sheep's milk, with at most 20 % goat's milk. It is made in Thessaly, Macedonia, Lesbos and Xanthi, and holds a Greek PDO. Turkish kaşar and Balkan kashkaval are the same family.

how.label: dip in hot water
how.text: Kasseri curd is left to acidify to about pH 5.2, then sliced and kneaded in hot water until it stretches. Kashkaval of the Balkans and kaşar of Turkey are the same kind of cheese.

steps.note: The curd is left to reach pH about 5.2.
Sliced, dipped in hot water and kneaded until it stretches to a 1 m thread.

processing.text: The curd is left to acidify before it is stretched in hot water.
